newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West spot power lifted by Northwest cold.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West spot power lifted by Northwest cold.

text.p: Cold weather in the U.S. Northwest boosted spot power prices throughout the West, market sources said Tuesday.
"What you are seeing is buying from the Northwest," said an Arizona trade source.
The Pacific Northwest was hit with heavy rain and wet snow starting Monday night, which pushed up electricity demand for heating loads.
At the same time, scattered power plant outages, both planned and unplanned, have tightened electricity supplies.

In the Northwest, the 700 MW unit 4 at the Colstrip coal-fired plant is due to restart Thursday, while the 550 MW unit 3 at the Jim Bridger plant in Wyoming was said to be scheduled for restart Tuesday.

In the Southwest, the 790 MW unit 1 at the Mohave coal-fired plant near Laughlin, Nev., is expected to be back up Wednesday, while unit 3 at the Four Corners coal-fired plant in Arizona is expected to restart Tuesday.

The 360 MW unit 1 at Springerville, Arizona, generating station was expected to be back to full power Tuesday, but the 720 MW unit 1 at the Navajo power plant remains down for maintenance work scheduled to end December 18.
Firm, on-peak power for Wednesday at the Palo Verde substation in Arizona was last quoted at $24.00-25.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), up from $20.00-22.00 for Tuesday.
Off-peak Palo Verde was quoted at $17.00-18.00, but traders said those prices were likely to drop as California utilities start bringing some gas-fired units on line.
On-peak Four Corners was also quoted at $24.00-25.00, while off-peak was at $16.00-17.00.

On-peak firm Mid-Columbia was quoted at $29.00-32.00 per MWh, while California-Oregon border (COB) power was quoted at $29.00-30.00, up from $25.00-26.00. Off-peak COB and Mid-Columbia were quoted at $19.00-21.00.
